findings.summary: The pages describe the 100,000-member union limit and recursion limits only on page 5, while the mental model on page 1 and cheat sheet on page 6 omit them, so the limits are missing from the revision summary.
findings.evidence: Several large slots can hit the 100,000-member union limit or slow the compiler
findings.fix: Add a cheat-sheet line: union limit 100,000 members; recursion depth 100, or 1000 when tail-recursive.

findings.summary: The Split example is shown with a bullet claiming H is the first character, but the page says nothing about recursion or the empty-string case, and the code appears after the idea only partly.
findings.evidence: In ${infer H}${infer T}, H is exactly the first character
findings.fix: Add one line: Split<''> is never, because the pattern needs at least one character for H.

findings.summary: One bullet holds two ideas (a pattern that accepts any matching string and the empty-string case) in a table cell.
findings.fix: Keep the Accepts cell to the examples and move 'user_${string} may be empty' to its own bullet.

findings.summary: The 'K & string' bullet mixes two ideas: templates build names, and why the intersection is needed.
findings.evidence: Template literals build names; K & string is needed as keyof may include number or symbol
findings.fix: Split into two bullets: 'Template literals build the new key names' and 'Use K & string because keyof may include number or symbol'.

findings.summary: The covariant/contravariant infer rule is stated without an example, so a skimming learner cannot apply it.
findings.evidence:
Several infer of one name in covariant slots → union
Several in contravariant slots → intersection
findings.fix: Add a short example, e.g. T extends { a: infer U; b: infer U } gives a union, while function parameters give an intersection.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "template", "literals").
findings.evidence: Unions in template literals multiply: large unions in several slots can hit the 100,000-member union limit or slow the compiler
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The recursion-depth table gives limits but not what counts as tail-recursive until a note below, and the bullet on modifiers packs several ideas.
findings.evidence:
Modifiers survive when iterating keyof T or a K extends keyof T
[K in SomeUnion] loses ? and readonly; [K in keyof T as ...] keeps them
findings.fix: Split into one bullet for when modifiers are kept and one for when they are lost, and place the tail-recursive definition before the table.

findings.summary: The Recipes list names types without showing them, and CamelCase says 'recursive infer on _' with no form, so it cannot be used as a cheat sheet.
findings.fix: Show the form: S extends `${infer H}_${infer R}` ? `${H}${CamelCase<Capitalize<R>>}` : S.
